evidence_items.publisher: The Motley Fool via Yahoo Finance

receipt.public_excerpt: about a fifth of its revenue in the first half of 2026 came from just two customers. Anthropic didn't name either company in its S-1 filing, but several industry reports have identified them as SpaceX (NASDAQ: SPCX) and Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT).

evidence_items.explanation: Shows that SpaceX (through Cursor) and Microsoft are reported to be Anthropic's two largest customers. This sets up the 'largest customers' part of the claim.

receipt.public_excerpt: It now owns xAI and Cursor, putting it in direct competition with Anthropic in foundation models through Grok and in AI coding tools through Cursor

evidence_items.explanation: Shows that SpaceX, a top customer through Cursor, owns and builds the rival Grok models. This matches 'SpaceX (which owns Cursor) has Grok'.

evidence_items.publisher: Investing.com via Yahoo Finance (citing The Information)

receipt.public_excerpt: Tech giants Meta Platforms and Microsoft are actively reducing their internal reliance on Anthropic's Claude AI technology as both companies steer employees toward their own in-house artificial intelligence tools

evidence_items.explanation: Shows that Meta and Microsoft are actively moving staff off Claude and onto their own tools. That fits 'discussing dropping their services', though it is a cut rather than a full exit.

evidence_items.publisher: Investing.com via Yahoo Finance (citing The Information)

receipt.public_excerpt: this reduction applies exclusively to internal operations; customer spending on Anthropic models via Microsoft's enterprise platforms continues to see steady growth.

evidence_items.explanation: Limits the 'dropping' part. Microsoft is cutting its own staff use, but resale of Claude through Microsoft platforms is growing. So Microsoft is not dropping Anthropic as a whole.

unresolved_gaps: The S-1 does not name its largest customers. Their identities rest on press reports.
No report found of Meta or Microsoft ending Claude use entirely. The reports describe cuts in internal use.
